headline_marked: Tk 105,580cr cost: [[Govt approves new pay scale]] for public servants
headline: Tk 105,580cr cost: Govt approves new pay scale for public servants
summary: The National Pay Scale 2026 will be implemented in four phases over two fiscal years to manage budget pressure and control inflation.
details: The government has approved the National Pay Scale 2026, which will be rolled out in four phases between July 2026 and January 2028 to ease the burden on the national budget and limit inflationary effects.
Basic salaries will be implemented in three phases from July 1, 2026, to July 1, 2027, while all allowances under the new structure will take effect from January 1, 2028.
Once fully implemented, the new pay scale will benefit approximately 24 lakh military and civilian employees, as well as about 925,000 pensioners and other eligible beneficiaries.
The revised structure is estimated to require an additional annual expenditure of Tk 105,580 crore, with funds allocated within the medium-term budget framework.
For the first time, the government is introducing a monthly allowance of Tk 3,000 for children with special needs of public servants.
Additionally, the mobile phone allowance, previously limited to Grade 5 employees, will now be extended to employees of all grades.
caption:
A new pay scale for public servants is coming, costing the government Tk 105,580 crore annually.

The government has approved the National Pay Scale 2026, which will be rolled out in four phases between July 2026 and January 2028 to ease the burden on the national budget and limit inflationary effects.

Basic salaries will be implemented in three phases from July 1, 2026, to July 1, 2027, while all allowances under the new structure will take effect from January 1, 2028.

Once fully implemented, the new pay scale will benefit approximately 24 lakh military and civilian employees, as well as about 925,000 pensioners and other eligible beneficiaries.

The revised structure is estimated to require an additional annual expenditure of Tk 105,580 crore, with funds allocated within the medium-term budget framework.

For the first time, the government is introducing a monthly allowance of Tk 3,000 for children with special needs of public servants.

Additionally, the mobile phone allowance, previously limited to Grade 5 employees, will now be extended to employees of all grades.

headline_marked: Tk 39 lakh mugging in Dhanmondi: [[Three arrested after firearm recovered]]
headline: Tk 39 lakh mugging in Dhanmondi: Three arrested after firearm recovered
summary: Police arrested three members of a mugging gang after they snatched cash from a person who had just withdrawn it from a bank.
details: Police have arrested three members of a mugging gang and recovered a firearm after they allegedly snatched Tk 39 lakh from a person in Dhaka’s Dhanmondi area yesterday.
The incident occurred when the victim, who was carrying the cash after withdrawing it from a bank, was targeted by three muggers on a motorcycle.
As the victim chased the suspects, one of the muggers fell off the motorcycle and was caught by locals near Dhanmondi Lake, along with a pistol.
Following a call to the National Emergency Service 999, Dhanmondi Police Station responded and arrested the first suspect, identified as Tanvir Abedin Jewel, 41.
Joint drives by local police and the Detective Branch (DB) subsequently led to the arrest of two other members of the gang.
Dhanmondi Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Emdadul Islam confirmed that a firearm and four rounds of bullets were recovered from the arrestees.
The snatched Tk 39 lakh has not yet been recovered, and police are continuing drives to trace the missing money and arrest other accomplices.
caption:
